label: Global JavaScript UDF/library
type: a JavaScript user-defined function or library created in the default: namespace, at the same level as buckets - available to every client with no scope restriction. Sibling of js-udf:scoped-function; a value of js-udf:udf-library's global/scoped choice.
recurrence_note: 7 files, shared-source verdict `divergent` (a real second author across cloud and server pages, not a republished duplicate) - discount rejected, raw file count stands.
evidence: A global library is created within the default: namespace, at the same level as the buckets in your database. A global library is available to all clients.

If you do not add a prefix before the library name in your SQL++ statement, the user-defined function will be created as a Global function. You cannot create another global function called GetBusinessDays on your cluster.
When you call a global function, any partial keyspace references within the function definition are resolved against the default: namespace, regardless of the current query context.
relates_to_competency_question: Can a JavaScript UDF be shared across every bucket in a cluster, or is it always scoped to one?
